summary: Implemented merge(base, override) in settings/merge.py per ADR-004: recursive dict merge, lists and scalars replaced, None removes keys at any level, and inputs are deep-copied so they are never mutated or aliased. The existing test passes (it failed with NotImplementedError before), and inline checks confirmed non-mutation, list replacement, nested None removal, and multi-layer load behaviour.
assumptions: ANALYSIS.md was not written: the operator instructions prohibit writing analysis .md files, and the write was refused. The pre-implementation analysis was completed in-session before any edit, and its conclusions are carried in this report's summary and assumptions instead.
A None override for a key absent from the base is dropped (no key is created), following ADR-004's 'removes the key from the result'.
A None nested inside a dict that is new in the override is also dropped, by building the new dict with the same merge rules.
Values are deep-copied so the result shares no mutable objects with cached layers (ADR-004 forbids mutating inputs; ADR-002 limits settings to JSON types).
No new tests were added; verification was done with the existing test plus an inline script.
